operative_context: Warehouse-facing identifier terminology and formal specification identifier terminology must be reconciled to prevent divergence
exceptions: Audit and privacy-preserving views may use alternative identifier styles if authorized reviewers have controlled access to identity-resolution paths
conflicts_or_obsolete: Divergent identifier terminology between specification and warehouse operations (barcode/serial code vs. formal item identifier)
Inconsistent identifier wording across specification, UI labels, and outbound notifications
Mismatch between business-oriented identifier format and scanner-friendly representation in warehouse workflows
notes: TARGET R38 addresses identifier alias consistency across the system. PRIMARY evidence E1 provides availability management context but does not directly address identifier consistency. CONTEXT evidence E2-E6 consistently highlight a core issue: identifier terminology diverges between formal specification, warehouse operations, UI labels, and notifications. E2 and E3 document backend and frontend concerns about identifier strategy alignment. E5 (logistics email) explicitly raises the barcode/serial code vs. formal identifier ambiguity. E4 and E6 extend the concern to notifications and audit reporting. The requirement appears to demand that all aliases and representations of item identifiers remain consistent across all system touchpoints, but the evidence reveals unresolved questions about whether a single identifier or multiple coordinated identifiers are intended. E7, E8, E9 provide tangential context on other identifier/consistency issues but are less directly relevant to item identifier alias consistency. Filtered abstract or low-relevance operative statements: Identifier aliases must be used consistently across all system layers (UI, backend, reporting, notifications, and audit views) | All user-facing displays, notifications, and exported artifacts must use the same identifier representation | Identifier representation must be consistent between persistence layer and presentation layer
